title: fix: send a default User-Agent from the computer's curl
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Routes the shell's outbound requests through an `Egress` entrypoint (`http-gateway` egress mode)
- Adds `User-Agent: pollinations-computer (+https://pollinations.ai)` only when the request has none; `curl -A` still wins
- Fixes 403s from APIs that require a User-Agent, e.g. api.github.com
- Test: default and custom User-Agent via an echo endpoint (17/17 pass)

gist.headline: Curl Gets a Name Tag
gist.blurb: The computer shell now introduces itself when it wanders onto the web. APIs that expect a User-Agent, including GitHub's, can stop mistaking a perfectly polite curl for suspicious weather.
gist.summary: Routed computer MCP shell requests through the http-gateway Egress entrypoint and added the default `User-Agent: pollinations-computer (+https://pollinations.ai)` when curl sends none, while preserving custom `curl -A` headers.
gist.impact: Computer MCP users can call User-Agent-requiring APIs such as `api.github.com` without 403s, and can still override the default identity with their own User-Agent.
